Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a matched frame cap gives perfectly smooth motion for a competitive shooter and avoids the GPU being pushed past its sweet spot. FSR upscaling from a slightly reduced render resolution keeps the image crisp enough for gameplay.

profiles.Summary: Overwatch® runs on the Steam Deck via Proton with a Playable rating, though it requires the Battle.net launcher to be set up first, which adds friction. The RDNA 2 GPU sits near the game's recommended tier, so medium-to-low settings at 1280x800 can sustain a stable 40–60 fps depending on the TDP budget.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs versus Deck GPU class (GTX 1650-equivalent) and general Proton/Battle.net launcher behaviour. On first launch, verify the Battle.net setup completes correctly, then check frame rate in a busy team fight and drop to Optimal or Max Battery settings if it stutters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render scale reduced and FSR applied on top to ease GPU load; 7 W TDP keeps thermals and fan noise low. Prioritises session length over visual fidelity — good for longer handheld play away from a charger.

KnownIssues: Requires Battle.net launcher setup through Proton, which can be finicky on first launch
Anti-cheat (WBAC) may cause occasional launch failures; workarounds vary by Proton version
Online-only game — any network or server issues will prevent play entirely
Controller aim assist may feel inconsistent in competitive modes compared to mouse/keyboard

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native resolution at uncapped TDP can push near 60 fps in most scenarios, though hectic team fights with heavy particle effects may dip into the high 40s. Dynamic Reflections and high shadow settings are the biggest GPU cost and are left at medium/off to maintain stability.

Optimal.Notes: A solid competitive experience at 60 fps with medium settings; shadows are dropped to Low as they are the biggest GPU cost in Overwatch 2. Reflections off and a slight render resolution reduction via Deck FSR keeps framing stable.

profiles.Summary: Overwatch 2 runs on the Steam Deck via Proton with a Playable rating, though it requires some initial setup and the Battle.net launcher adds friction. The RDNA 2 GPU sits right at the recommended spec tier, allowing medium settings at a stable 60 fps with some tuning effort.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended specs (Deck GPU ≈ GTX 1650 class, matching the recommended tier), ProtonDB platinum/gold trend, and known Overwatch 2 graphics options. On first run, check frame stability during a full team fight and lower Shadow Detail and Effects Detail first if fps dips below your cap.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping render scale to 75% internally and letting Deck FSR handle upscaling keeps GPU load low enough for 8 W TDP. This profile sacrifices visual fidelity significantly but is playable for casual matches.

KnownIssues: Battle.net launcher must be navigated with controller or the game launched via a workaround — initial setup can be cumbersome on Deck
Anti-cheat (Warden) occasionally causes launch failures; GE-Proton or Proton Experimental may be required to get the game running
Text and UI elements can be very small at 1280x800 without adjusting in-game UI scale
Online-only game requires a stable network connection; Wi-Fi latency on Deck can affect competitive play

MaxPerformance.Notes: Targeting 90 Hz is ambitious; expect 60-80 fps in practice with dips during intense team fights at high settings. Reflections remain off as they are disproportionately expensive and rarely noticed in fast-paced play.
